paragraphs: One might argue that using computer can help people see historical objects and works of art, so public museums and art galleries will be no longer needed. In this essay, however, I am to refute this school of thought.

Admittedly, technology has beneficial cultural and historical experience. This is predicated on the assumption that technology brings high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, this enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail and without living home. For example, Louvre museum, which one of the most famous museum in the world, has offers some of websites that helps people around the world explore masterpieces and with no cost or a little payment. Those help people who cannot afford or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are essential. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artworks in person, this evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. A clear example is that experienced about a historical museum, you can see and touch ancient artefacts in your own, have direct sensory engagement, this are things that online experience does not have. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region, this is a magnet for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that technology can help people get a good experience about cultural and historical. However I believe that museums and galleries are necessary and cannot be replace.

paragraphs: One might argue that school students who show the best results should have rewards; however, others think that rewarding students who show improvements is more necessary. In my perspective, I think that school should reward both.

Admittedly, rewarding best results students is normally. Initially, students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, so they deserve their praises and privileges, this may encourage these student and others to study harder to win the reward and propel towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded, so students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition will enable them to achieve success in later time.

However, improvements students should also have rewards. In real life, if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, it may cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals and prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, so they would gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves irrespective of how well they have been or are performing, this helps the constant desire to outdo themselves and even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that school should reward both students who show the best academic results and improvements.
review.overall: Em đã bám đúng hướng chính của đề: công nhận học sinh có thành tích cao và ủng hộ việc thưởng cả học sinh có tiến bộ. Hai thân bài đã có hầu hết các ý Cô giao, đặc biệt là tác động của cạnh tranh và việc động viên người học ở mọi trình độ. Tuy nhiên, nhiều câu bị nối bằng dấu phẩy hoặc ghép sai cấu trúc, nên chuỗi lập luận khó theo dõi. Em cần viết lại bài, trước hết hoàn chỉnh câu chủ đề rồi tách và kiểm tra từng mệnh đề trước khi nối chúng.

paragraphs: Some people argue that schools should reward students who achieve the best academic results, whereas others believe that students who make progress deserve greater recognition. From my perspective, schools should reward both groups.

Admittedly, there are sound reasons to reward students who excel in their studies. Since they have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. Such rewards may encourage both these students and their peers to study harder, thereby improving overall academic achievement. Furthermore, competition exists in many aspects of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. If students become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, they may be better prepared for success later in life.

However, schools should also reward students who show improvement. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, other students may feel that their efforts are futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may become overwhelmed and disheartened, gradually losing the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvement can encourage all students to be diligent and to keep improving themselves irrespective of their current performance. This constant desire to outdo themselves may be more valuable than the determination to defeat others in competition.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that schools should reward both students who achieve the best academic results and those who make progress.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is often argued that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others believe that individuals need to be free to take part in any sports or activities. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited since even a minor error, may cause the death of participants, skydiving, which can immediately kill the participant when someone makes mistake, is an example. However, the ban is not possible, initially, in some remote locations, say mountain cliffs, there are minimal surveillance or control, so dangerous happens frequently, with no following. Furthermore, prohibiting extreme sports is unrealistic because of the fact that a police officer can not follow every individual. This make a prohibition exist only on paper and drive practice underground, so it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

In my perspective, people should be permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For example, if individual want deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping, they need to register to reputable club [chưa đọc rõ] have appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Another example is that newbie people would be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur, so they can recognise dangers and respond appropriately. This proper training and necessary precautions can bring safer participation and no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I strongly believe that banning neither practical nor effective, while freedom to choose, under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

review.overall: Em nêu đủ hai phía, chọn quyền tham gia có điều kiện và viết trọn bốn phần. Các ví dụ nhảy dù, câu lạc bộ và chuyên gia đi cùng đúng đề. Tuy nhiên, bài còn cẩu thả ở khâu dựng câu và tự soát: 'This make a prohibition exist...' sai hòa hợp, 'so it harder...' thiếu động từ, và 'banning neither practical nor effective' thiếu is. Về lập luận, giám sát ít không chứng minh tai nạn xảy ra thường xuyên như câu 'so dangerous happens frequently'; em cần gắn nó với khó thực thi lệnh cấm. Mức vận dụng cấu trúc đã học còn rất yếu ở các câu chủ chốt. Em phải viết lại bài, giải thích được mỗi quan hệ nhân quả và kiểm tra chủ ngữ–động từ trước khi đối chiếu bản chữa. paragraphs: It is often argued that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others believe that individuals need to be free to take part in any sports or activities. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited since even a minor error may cause the death of participants; an error in skydiving can be fatal, for example. However, the ban is difficult to enforce. Initially, these sports take place in remote locations, say mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. Furthermore, prohibiting extreme sports is unrealistic given that a police officer cannot follow every individual. This means that a prohibition may exist only on paper and drive the practice underground, making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

From my perspective, people should be permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For example, if individuals want to try deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping, they need to register with a reputable club that can provide appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Another example is that beginners would be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur, so that they can recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Proper training and necessary precautions can make participation safer. Nevertheless, no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, I strongly believe that banning is neither practical nor effective, while freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: It is often argued that children can learn through trial and error, while others think adults should help them avoid mistakes. From my perspective, freedom to make mistakes should be encouraged, provided that the errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, those who favour preventing children’s mistakes have several reasons. Initially, many mistakes are avoidable: children do not need to get hurt by knives, fire or electricity to learn to be careful. Furthermore, adults have a duty to shield children from harm, and by forestalling such mistakes, parents can fulfil that duty. Moreover, pre-emptively helping children gives parents peace of mind since they know they have done their best to protect and raise them.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasoning. First, parents cannot be around their children all the time; therefore, children will experiment with new things and inevitably make some mistakes. Second, children learn invaluable lessons through trial and error, and these can stand them in good stead later in life. Finally, shielding children from everything can make them depend too much on their parents, which is an undesirable trait.

In conclusion, it seems to me that allowing children to learn from mistakes may help prepare them for the future, provided that parents intervene or give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail that future.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart shows carbon emissions from gas, oil and coal in the UK at five points between 1990 and 2010, measured in millions of tons.

Overall, gas emissions rose throughout the period and became the largest of the three from 2000 onwards. Coal emissions declined steadily, while oil emissions fell overall despite a temporary rise around 2000.

In 1990, coal generated approximately 310 million tons of emissions, compared with around 270 million tons from oil and 220 million tons from gas. By 1995, gas had risen to roughly 270 million tons, nearly matching coal at 280 million tons; oil had fallen to about 240 million tons. In 2000, gas reached 300 million tons and overtook both coal and oil, at approximately 250 and 260 million tons respectively.

From 2000 onwards, gas continued to increase, reaching around 320 million tons in 2010. By contrast, oil dropped from approximately 260 to 210 million tons, while coal fell from about 250 to 190 million tons over the same decade. Coal was therefore the smallest source at the end of the period.

review.overall: Em đã viết đủ hai hướng và cho thấy quan điểm các môn đều quan trọng. Cần thay ý lặp lại bằng một ví dụ lịch sử và một ví dụ khoa học cụ thể, rồi giải thích mỗi ví dụ chứng minh lợi ích gì. Trước khi nộp, em nên kiểm tra động từ sau chủ ngữ số nhiều và bỏ kiểu so sánh “more better”.

criteria.label: TR
criteria.comment: Em nêu lập trường cả hai nhóm môn quan trọng và có bàn đến hai phía. Tuy nhiên lý do về lịch sử chủ yếu lặp “biết quá khứ”; ví dụ physics/chemical phát triển từ mathematics không giải thích được vai trò của môn lịch sử, còn đoạn khoa học lặp lại ý “rất quan trọng” mà thiếu dẫn chứng.

criteria.label: CC
criteria.comment: Có bốn đoạn đúng chức năng, nhưng câu trong thân bài nối lỏng và “On the other hand” dùng lần thứ hai bên trong chính đoạn khoa học khiến quan hệ giữa các ý không rõ.

criteria.label: LR
criteria.comment: Có vốn từ cơ bản đúng chủ đề như past, science, technology, ocean, space. Nhưng từ lặp nhiều và kết hợp sai “more better machine”, “very development”, “other revel” gây khó hiểu.

criteria.label: GRA
criteria.comment: Nhiều lỗi hòa hợp chủ-vị, cấu trúc make, so sánh và câu phức xuất hiện liên tục; một số câu rất khó phân tích dù vẫn nhận được ý chung.

paragraphs.text: Some people believe that history is one of the most important school subjects, while others think science and technology matter more in the modern world. I believe that all three deserve attention because they offer different kinds of knowledge.

History helps students understand how their countries developed. Learning about past events can show them why important decisions were made and how those decisions affected ordinary people. For example, a lesson on a country’s struggle for independence may explain why its citizens value sovereignty today. Without such knowledge, young people may find it harder to understand their national traditions or appreciate the efforts of earlier generations. History can also teach them to examine sources carefully rather than accept every claim they hear. These are benefits that a science lesson may not provide in the same way.

Science and technology are also important because they help people solve practical problems. Scientific study teaches students to test ideas and use evidence. It can prepare some of them to develop machines that explore deep oceans or space, places that are difficult for people to reach directly. Technology lessons can also help students use digital tools effectively in study and work. For instance, an engineer who understands physics and computing may design equipment that makes research safer and more accurate. These skills matter to both individuals and society, but they serve a different purpose from the cultural knowledge gained through history.

In conclusion, history teaches students about the past and their communities, while science and technology equip them to investigate and improve the world around them. No single subject is necessarily more important in every situation, so schools should give students opportunities to study each area.
